notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Tuning: a missed restart no longer counts as a failed test. When the modchip misses the
tuner's restart, the console starts the Nintendo logo and the HOME Menu, and that setting was
never tested. The tuner now sees that and tests it again, instead of failing it and settling on
a lower RAM speed or a smaller undervolt than the console can do.

Tuning: in hekate's More Configs, SCCM Scratch is now called Retry Last Test. If the HOME Menu
starts instead of hekate, turn the console off and on and pick Retry Last Test. After a frozen,
garbled or black screen, hold POWER and pick Continue Tuning, as before. The Overclocking Setup
guide shows both.

Tuning: the progress screen shows on every test. It sometimes failed to start, leaving a black
screen with the game playing, so a running test looked the same as a hung one.

Mario Kart Wii port: a game that closed a few seconds into every launch starts again. Its
settings file pointed at a folder with no disc in it, as one made on a PC or by Wheel Wizard
does; the launcher now puts the path back before each start. When the game stops on an error,
the message says why.

SCCM Retro app: a card that already has a Linux system, like L4T Ubuntu or Switchroot Fedora,
can take SCCM Retro in its place. Install asks first, and that choice erases the Linux
partition; Android, Lakka and other entries stay. A card with Android left on it is now named
as such instead of "already has a Linux partition", and a Switchroot Fedora card is no longer
mistaken for SCCM Retro.

Not tried yet: the tuning changes in a real tuning session (they pass the tuner's own tests),
and installing in place of a Linux system on a real card (tested on a simulated card).

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
